bai.ten: Wave function and probability: an electron in a box
bai.moTa: Drag the well wall, locate nodes, and sample positions.
bai.yChinh: The two walls select discrete standing waves. The squared magnitude of the wave function gives probability density.
bai.giaiThich: The box is a one-dimensional infinite well. Blue shows the real wave function at a chosen phase; gold shows density. Dots are samples from independently prepared electrons in the same state.
bai.conSo.1: At n = 2 the box center is a node.
bai.conSo.2: Doubling the width reduces the ground energy to 1/4 of its original value.
bai.hieuDung: A negative amplitude still gives positive density. Even with no force inside the well, the lowest energy is nonzero.
bai.nguon: Prepared by Trí Lữ. Model and solutions follow OpenStax, University Physics, Vol. 3, §7.4, and Griffiths and Schroeter, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics, Ch. 2.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.1: Infer allowed wavelengths from the boundaries.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.2: Use area under the density to predict detection frequencies.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.3: Predict the energy after changing the width.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.1.noiDung:
An electron is free between ideal walls. Infinite walls force its wave function to vanish at both ends. A wave with finite amplitude at a wall violates the model’s boundary condition.

A string fixed at both ends helps visualize the boundary. A real string moves through space, whereas the electron has an amplitude associated with each position. As you move the wall, track where the blue curve meets the axis and where its magnitude peaks.

$$ \psi(0)=\psi(L)=0 $$

+++ A closer look · Boundaries of the well
Horizontal distance is position. Curve height gives the value of a function; the raised graph can be rotated for inspection.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Select ground state|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.2.noiDung:
In the ground state half a wavelength fits inside. The next state fits one whole wavelength. Each additional half wavelength adds a lobe.

Hold the wall still and count the segments lying completely above or below the blue axis. Each segment runs between adjacent nodes. Adding a fraction of a half wavelength would leave the end away from the right wall. This is why the allowed indices are discrete.

$$ L=n\lambda_n/2 $$

+++ A closer look · Allowed n
The index n is a positive integer. Setting it to zero gives the zero function everywhere, which cannot be normalized to one particle.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Switch to n = 2|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.noiDung:
Blue may dip below its axis. Squaring its magnitude gives the nonnegative gold density. At a node the density remains zero however many preparations are measured.

Compare the middle of a positive lobe with the mirror point of a negative lobe. Detectors covering equally wide small intervals there give nearly equal frequencies. If the blue curve suggests fewer detections on its negative side, check the gold density and the dots.

$$ \rho(x)=|\psi_n(x)|^2 $$

+++ A closer look · Read the midpoint
Set n = 2 and drag the probe. The two lobes have opposite signs yet their densities are symmetric about the center.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Select a central node|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.thuThach.de: Drag the probe to the central node at n = 2, within 0.03 box widths.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.4.noiDung:
Mark an interval of positions. Detection probability is the area under the density over that interval. A single density reading does not determine the area.

The probe sets the interval’s right edge while its left edge stays at the wall. Moving the probe right can only increase the enclosed probability. The same displacement adds more area near a lobe than near a node. Drag slowly across both regions to check.

$$ P(0<x<b)=\int_0^b|\psi_n(x)|^2\,dx $$

+++ A closer look · Changing units
Density has units of inverse length. Multiplying by a length element and integrating leaves a dimensionless probability. The full box has probability one.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Inspect half the box|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.5.noiDung:
More lobes imply a larger characteristic momentum. Kinetic energy is quadratic in momentum, so energy rises with the square of n.

Read the level index and then the energy in units of the reference ground energy. Raising the index by one adds one lobe, yet the jump in energy grows for larger indices. A spatially smooth wave inside the box is consistent with a discrete sequence of energies.

$$ E_n=n^2h^2/(8mL^2) $$

+++ A closer look · Spacing between levels
At fixed width the first energies are in the ratio 1, 4, 9. Gaps between neighboring levels grow. For an electron in a box $1\,\mathrm{nm}$ wide, $E_1=h^2/(8mL^2)\approx0{,}376\,\mathrm{eV}$, so $E_2\approx1{,}50\,\mathrm{eV}$ and $E_3\approx3{,}38\,\mathrm{eV}$.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Select n = 3|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.6.noiDung:
Drag the right wall outward and compare the ground energy with a 1 nm reference box. At fixed n a wider box admits a longer wavelength and lower kinetic energy.

Keep the probe at the same fractional position as the wall moves. The lobe count and probability to its left stay fixed, while density peaks drop because the same area spreads over more length. Check whole-box probability if the lower peak looks like a lost electron.

$$ E_n(2L)/E_n(L)=1/4 $$

+++ A closer look · Compare two preparations
Changing the wall prepares the eigenstate again in the new well. A suddenly moving physical wall can produce a superposition of energy states.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Restore the 1 nm box|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.6.thuThach.de: Drag the wall until the ground energy is 1/4 of the reference value, within 0.02 reference units.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.noiDung:
Bright dots represent position measurements on independently prepared particles. Over many trials they cluster at density lobes. A click marks a detection; at high rates only a subset sounds.

Two runs starting with clean screens usually have different first few dots. What can be compared is the fraction falling in the same interval. As the sample grows, frequencies typically approach the theoretical area; a short run cannot reproduce a full distribution.

$$ f_j=N_j/N $$

+++ A closer look · What is sampled?
Dots are separated in depth solely for visibility. Only their coordinate along the box is a one-dimensional measurement outcome.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Clear samples and count again|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.8.noiDung:
An energy eigenstate has time-independent density. Its whole wave function gains the same phase; taking the squared magnitude removes it.

To see a time-dependent phase effect one could compare different energy components in a superposition. This experiment prepares a single level each time, so the density lobes do not shuttle across the box. On the table the blue curve pulses while the gold density stays still; what changes from run to run is the set of newly detected dots.

$$ \Psi(x,t)=\psi_n(x)e^{-iE_nt/\hbar} $$

+++ A closer look · Compare with detections
In this step the blue curve is the real part of $\Psi$: it swells and shrinks in place with the phase $e^{-iE_nt/\hbar}$, slowed enormously on screen. The nodes stay put and the gold density does not change. This overall phase cannot be detected by a position measurement. Repeated measurement frequencies fluctuate about the probability. These statistical variations have a different origin from phase evolution.
+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Resample at n = 3|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.8.thuThach.de: At n = 3 drag the probe to the left interior node within 0.025 box widths.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.8.thuThach.goiY: Find the first change of sign after the left wall.
bai.baiGiang.congThuc.3.y: The reference uses n = 1, L = 1 nm.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.hoi: At fixed L, raising n from 1 to 3 multiplies the energy by what factor?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.2.hoi: What is the central density at n = 2?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.2.giai: The center is a wave-function node.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.hoi: At fixed n, doubling L scales the energy by what factor?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.giai: Energy scales inversely with width squared.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.hoi: Why can many particles be found under a negative lobe?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.dap: Density is the squared magnitude, so the magnitude of the lobe matters.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.5.hoi: What determines probability in an interval?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.5.dap: The integral of density over that interval.
